title: Who's the lightweight?
setting: Friday night at a small izakaya. Yuki and her old friend Kenta are out drinking together for the first time. She warns him she can't hold her drink. He says he can hold his, and it never shows on his face. A few glasses of strong sake later, things look rather different.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: kanpai! sou ieba, yuki to nomi ni itta koto, nakatta yo ne.
lines.ja: 乾杯！そういえば、ユキと飲みに行ったこと、なかったよね。
lines.kana: かんぱい！そういえば、ゆきとのみにいったこと、なかったよね。
lines.english: Cheers! Come to think of it, we've never been out drinking together before, have we?

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: un. gohan ni wa yoku iku kedo ne. watashi, osake yowai kara.
lines.ja: うん。ご飯にはよく行くけどね。私、お酒弱いから。
lines.kana: うん。ごはんにはよくいくけどね。わたし、おさけよわいから。
lines.english: Right. We go out to eat a lot, though. I'm a lightweight, you see.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: sou na n da. boku wa kekkou osake tsuyoi yo. nanbai nonde mo, kao ni denai n da.
lines.ja: そうなんだ。僕はけっこうお酒強いよ。何杯飲んでも、顔に出ないんだ。
lines.kana: そうなんだ。ぼくはけっこうおさけつよいよ。なんばいのんでも、かおにでないんだ。
lines.english: Oh, really? I can hold my drink pretty well. No matter how many I have, it never shows on my face.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: ii naa. jaa, watashi wa kore ippai dake ni shitoku ne.
lines.ja: いいなあ。じゃあ、私はこれ一杯だけにしとくね。
lines.kana: いいなあ。じゃあ、わたしはこれいっぱいだけにしとくね。
lines.english: Lucky you. Well, I'll stick to just this one glass.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: e, kore mo nonde mite yo. kono osake, chotto tsuyoi kedo, oishii yo.
lines.ja: え、これも飲んでみてよ。このお酒、ちょっと強いけど、おいしいよ。
lines.kana: え、これものんでみてよ。このおさけ、ちょっとつよいけど、おいしいよ。
lines.english: Oh, come on, try this one too. This sake's a bit strong, but it's really good.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: jaa, chotto dake. a, honto da. oishii!
lines.ja: じゃあ、ちょっとだけ。あ、ほんとだ。おいしい！
lines.kana: じゃあ、ちょっとだけ。あ、ほんとだ。おいしい！
lines.english: Okay, just a little. Oh, you're right. It's good!

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.ja: でしょ？じゃあ、もう一杯頼もう。
lines.kana: でしょ？じゃあ、もういっぱいたのもう。
lines.english: Told you. Let's order another, then.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: kenta, mou yonhai mo nonderu yo. kao ni deteru kedo, daijoubu?
lines.ja: ケンタ、もう四杯も飲んでるよ。顔に出てるけど、大丈夫？
lines.kana: けんた、もうよんはいものんでるよ。かおにでてるけど、だいじょうぶ？
lines.english: Kenta, you've had four already. It's showing on your face. Are you okay?

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: daijoubu, daijoubu. a, chotto tabako sutte kite mo ii?
lines.ja: 大丈夫、大丈夫。あ、ちょっとタバコ吸ってきてもいい？
lines.kana: だいじょうぶ、だいじょうぶ。あ、ちょっとたばこすってきてもいい？
lines.english: I'm fine, I'm fine. Oh, mind if I pop out for a smoke?

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: e, kenta, tabako suu no? shiranakatta.
lines.ja: え、ケンタ、タバコ吸うの？知らなかった。
lines.kana: え、けんた、たばこすうの？しらなかった。
lines.english: Wait, Kenta, you smoke? I had no idea.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: itsumo wa suwanai yo. demo, osake ga hairu to, tabako suitaku naru n da yo ne.
lines.ja: いつもは吸わないよ。でも、お酒が入ると、タバコ吸いたくなるんだよね。
lines.kana: いつもはすわないよ。でも、おさけがはいると、たばこすいたくなるんだよね。
lines.english: Not usually. But once I've had a few, I start wanting a cigarette.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: hee. demo kenta, honto ni osake tsuyoi no? watashi, mou gohai nonderu kedo.
lines.ja: へえ。でもケンタ、ほんとにお酒強いの？私、もう五杯飲んでるけど。
lines.kana: へえ。でもけんた、ほんとにおさけつよいの？わたし、もうごはいのんでるけど。
lines.english: Huh. But Kenta, can you really hold your drink? I've already had five, you know.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: e! gohai? osake yowai tte itta jan! uso tsuita no?
lines.ja: え！五杯？お酒弱いって言ったじゃん！嘘ついたの？
lines.kana: え！ごはい？おさけよわいっていったじゃん！うそついたの？
lines.english: What? Five? You said you were a lightweight! Were you lying?

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: gomen. shigoto no hito to nomi ni iku to, itsumo osake yowai n desu tte iu n da.
lines.ja: ごめん。仕事の人と飲みに行くと、いつも「お酒弱いんです」って言うんだ。
lines.kana: ごめん。しごとのひととのみにいくと、いつも「おさけよわいんです」っていうんだ。
lines.english: Sorry. Whenever I go drinking with people from work, I always tell them I'm not much of a drinker.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: sokka. jaa, kore kara wa issho ni nomi ni ikeru ne!
lines.ja: そっか。じゃあ、これからは一緒に飲みに行けるね！
lines.kana: そっか。じゃあ、これからはいっしょにのみにいけるね！
lines.english: I see. Well then, from now on we can go out drinking together!

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: kenta wa? osake tsuyoi n ja nakatta no?
lines.ja: ケンタは？お酒強いんじゃなかったの？
lines.kana: けんたは？おさけつよいんじゃなかったの？
lines.english: What about you? Weren't you the one who could hold his drink?

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: boku ga yowai n ja nai yo. kono osake ga tsuyoi n da yo.
lines.ja: 僕が弱いんじゃないよ。このお酒が強いんだよ。
lines.kana: ぼくがよわいんじゃないよ。このおさけがつよいんだよ。
lines.english: I'm not the lightweight here. This sake is just strong.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: hai hai. mizu nonde. kondo wa, gohan ni ikou ne.
lines.ja: はいはい。水飲んで。今度は、ご飯に行こうね。
lines.kana: はいはい。みずのんで。こんどは、ごはんにいこうね。
lines.english: Yeah, yeah. Drink some water. Next time, let's go out to eat instead.

choices.english: Yuki gets drunk on Kenta's strong sake, so Kenta orders her some water, and they agree to just go out to eat next time.
Kenta wants to smoke, but Yuki won't let him, so they leave the bar and go out to eat instead.
Kenta boasts that he can hold his drink, but it soon shows on his face. Yuki, who said she was a lightweight, drinks more than him and is fine.

questions.explanation: Lines 2-3 set it up: Yuki says she's a lightweight (watashi, osake yowai kara), and Kenta boasts that he can hold his drink and it never shows on his face. By line 8 he's had four glasses and it's showing. In line 12 Yuki has had five and is fine. In line 14 she admits that osake yowai n desu is just what she tells people from work, and in line 17 Kenta blames the sake. A gets them the wrong way round: Yuki is the one telling Kenta to drink water (line 18). B: Kenta asks to pop out for a smoke (line 9), but nobody leaves. Going out to eat is only Yuki's idea for next time (line 18).

questions.english: Kenta says: "You free tonight? Let's go somewhere." Suggest going out for drinks.
questions.ja: 今晩ひま？どこか行こうよ。
questions.kana: こんばんひま？どこかいこうよ。
questions.romaji: konban hima? doko ka ikou yo.
questions.answer: Suggest going out for a drink with nomi ni iku: nomi ni ikanai? or nomi ni ikou yo. You don't need to say osake, because nomi already means alcohol.

modelAnswers.romaji: ii ne. jaa, nomi ni ikanai?
modelAnswers.ja: いいね。じゃあ、飲みに行かない？
modelAnswers.english: Sounds good. Want to go for a drink, then?

modelAnswers.romaji: hima da yo. hisashiburi ni, nomi ni ikou yo.
modelAnswers.ja: ひまだよ。久しぶりに、飲みに行こうよ。
modelAnswers.english: I'm free. Let's go for a drink, it's been ages.

questions.explanation: Kenta uses it in line 1 (yuki to nomi ni itta koto, nakatta yo ne) and line 15 (issho ni nomi ni ikeru ne), and Yuki uses it in line 14 (shigoto no hito to nomi ni iku to). On its own, nomi already means drinking alcohol, so you don't need osake. It's the drinking version of gohan ni iku, which Yuki uses for going out to eat (lines 2 and 18). Just nomou (let's drink) is what you'd say with a glass in front of you. For a plan to go out, use nomi ni iku.

questions.english: Kenta wants a cigarette. What does he ask Yuki?
questions.ja: ケンタさんは、ユキさんに何と聞きましたか？
questions.kana: けんたさんは、ゆきさんになんとききましたか？
questions.romaji: kenta-san wa, yuki-san ni nan to kikimashita ka?

choices.english: Okay if I go and smoke?
choices.romaji: chotto kitsuen shite kite mo ii?

choices.english: Mind if I pop out for a smoke?
choices.romaji: chotto tabako sutte kite mo ii?

choices.english: Mind if I go have a cigarette?
choices.romaji: chotto tabako nonde kite mo ii?

questions.explanation: Line 9: chotto tabako sutte kite mo ii? Yuki answers with the same verb in line 10 (tabako suu no?), and Kenta uses it again in line 11 (tabako suitaku naru). In Japanese you breathe tobacco in: tabako (o) suu. A, kitsuen suru, is the dictionary word for 'smoke', but it belongs on signs and forms (kitsuen seki, a smoking seat; kin'en, no smoking). Said to a friend over drinks, it sounds like a notice on the wall. C, tabako o nomu, is an old way of saying it that some elderly people still use. Today it sounds dated, and it's an easy slip here because everyone is drinking (nomu). Tobacco takes suu.

questions.english: At a work drinking party, your manager Tanaka-san offers: "How about another one?" Turn it down politely by saying you can't hold your drink.
questions.kana: もういっぱい、どうですか？
questions.answer: Say that you are the weak one: osake yowai n desu. Use the polite form with your manager, and keep yourself as the topic, not the drink.

modelAnswers.ja: すみません、お酒弱いんです。
modelAnswers.english: Sorry, I'm not much of a drinker.

modelAnswers.romaji: arigatou gozaimasu. demo, osake ga yowai n de, ippai dake ni shitokimasu.
modelAnswers.ja: ありがとうございます。でも、お酒が弱いんで、一杯だけにしときます。
modelAnswers.english: Thank you, but I can't really hold my drink, so I'll stop at one.

questions.explanation: Yuki says it about herself in line 2 (watashi, osake yowai kara). Line 14 shows it's the polite line she uses with people from work: osake yowai n desu. Saying you're weak with alcohol is the standard, gentle way to turn down another glass, and people usually accept it without fuss. amari nomenai n desu (I can't drink much) is correct but blunter. Keep yourself as the topic. With the drink as the subject, kono osake yowai would mean the drink is weak, just as kono osake ga tsuyoi in line 17 is about the sake, not about Kenta. osake ni yowai is fine too.

questions.english: Late in the evening, Yuki asks Kenta "honto ni osake tsuyoi no?" What is she asking?
questions.ja: ユキさんは、ケンタさんに「ほんとにお酒強いの？」と聞きました。どういう意味ですか？
questions.kana: ゆきさんは、けんたさんに「ほんとにおさけつよいの？」とききました。どういういみですか？
questions.romaji: yuki-san wa, kenta-san ni honto ni osake tsuyoi no to kikimashita. dou iu imi desu ka?

choices.english: Whether he can really drink a lot without it getting to him.
Whether the sake he ordered is really as strong as he says.
Whether he really prefers strong drinks.

questions.explanation: When a person is the topic, osake (ga) tsuyoi means that person can hold their drink. Kenta boasts about it in line 3 (boku wa kekkou osake tsuyoi yo). By line 8 he's on his fourth glass and it shows on his face, so in line 12 Yuki, who has had five, doubts him. In line 16 she throws it back at him: osake tsuyoi n ja nakatta no? B is the other tsuyoi: when the drink is the subject, kono osake tsuyoi means the drink itself is strong. Kenta says that in line 5 (kono osake, chotto tsuyoi kedo, oishii yo) and blames it in line 17 (kono osake ga tsuyoi n da yo), but Yuki's question is about him. C: liking something would be suki. tsuyoi here is about how well he handles alcohol, not his taste.

newWords.english: counter for glasses and cups (ippai = one glass, nanbai = how many glasses, yonhai = four, gohai = five)
show on your face (kao ni denai = it doesn't show; kao ni deteru = it's showing)
have had a drink or two (literally, the alcohol is in you)
